transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-05-14 15:00 PDT
Duration: 57 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: enabled
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Kumar (Nova - Lead Eng), Carlos Mendes (Nova - CTO), Aisha Rahman (Nova - DevOps), Sam Lee (Nova - PM)

Summary: Quick SDK integration walkthrough focusing on Python and TypeScript quickstarts, auth options (API keys v SSO), environment setup for Redwood API and Redwood Dedicated considerations, and next steps to run benchmarks. Customer is evaluating hosted API first but wants options for Dedicated/VPC.

Topics covered: SDK quickstart (py/ts), auth + KMS, env vars and secrets management, sample request payloads, batching and cost tradeoffs, running a small benchmark, next steps for security docs.

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Lena, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Priya: Good, thanks. Heard good things. Quick note we have about 50 min then Sam has to jump at 40.
[00:14] Jordan: Great, we'll prioritize the SDK quickstart and env setup then the benchmark plan.
[00:22] Lena: Cool, I'll start with a quick demo of the Python quickstart, then show the TypeScript flow and how auth and envs fit in. This is more of a walkthrough than a live code debug but we can drop a repo link.
[00:37] Lena: (screen share) So here is the repo, redwood-sdk-quickstart. We have two folders: python/ and typescript/. The python README shows pip install redwood-inference, set REDWOOD_API_KEY as an env var, and then a small snippet: from redwood import RedwoodClient; client = RedwoodClient(); client.generate(...).
[01:05] Priya: Quick question — we use SSO and rotate keys via KMS. How do you recommend we do auth?
[01:12] Jordan: Good question. For initial eval, API keys are simplest — you set REDWOOD_API_KEY in your CI or env. For Dedicated/Private we support SSO/SSO+RBAC and KMS integration; we can provide the security whitepaper.
[01:28] Carlos: When you say KMS, you mean we can bring our own KMS for key wrapping?
[01:33] Lena: Yes, BYOK supported with Dedicated and Private. For hosted we manage keys but we can integrate with customer KMS through an HSM/KMS bridge for enterprise contracts. The transcript might read K V cash sometimes but it's KV cache — sorry for the t-run.
[01:50] Aisha: Also curious about env setup — do you support dotenv or vault? We use Hashi.
[01:55] Lena: We show a sample .env for quickstart but for prod we recommend Vault; the SDK has a small adapter. We'll include sample env var names: REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_ENV (staging/prod), REDWOOD_REGION. For VPC/Dedicated you also add REDWOOD_ENDPOINT to point to the private endpoint.
[02:18] Jordan: I'll add that to the notes.
[02:22] Lena: Now for TypeScript, same pattern: npm install @redwood/inference, set process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, then const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); await client.generate({ model: 'rw-1-large', prompt: '...' });
[02:48] Sam: Are there official SDKs for both node and browser? We plan to run inference server-side only.
[02:53] Lena: We have Node and browser builds but recommend server-side for secrets. Browser SDK is limited to embedding flows with a proxy.
[03:03] Priya: Can you demo a streaming response? That matters for UX latency.
[03:09] Lena: Sure, in Python you can call client.stream_generate(...) and get token deltas; same in TypeScript via an async iterator. We'll share snippets. Note: streaming goes over chunked HTTP/WS depending on region and product (hosted vs dedicated).
[03:36] [05:15] Lena: Switching topics: batching and cost controls. For Nova's use-case — mostly transactional replies with ~60-120 tokens per call — you can tune max_tokens and batching. Redwood Optimize will recommend batching windows and quantization profiles.
[05:40] Carlos: We care about tail latency; what SLOs do you typically hit?
[05:46] Jordan: Hosted gets p95 in the 80-130ms for small models; larger models are higher; Dedicated has predictable p95 depending on GPU profile. We'll share our perf deck.
[06:05] Priya: Any gotchas around KV cache and session state for chat? We saw something about KV cache eviction.
[06:12] Lena: Yes, KV cache matters for chat — we cache prefixes and manage KV eviction; for longer sessions we recommend explicit cache pinning or windowed prompts. Sometimes transcripts show "KV cash" which is just transcription error.
[06:30] Aisha: For the quickstart, will you provide a docker-compose dev environment?
[06:36] Lena: There's a docker-compose for local dev that sets up the sample app with env file and a simple proxy for API key rotation. We'll attach the link.
[07:05] Jordan: Security checklist — Nova listed SOC 2, SSO with SAML, KMS, audit logs. We support all of those; I'll send the security pack.
[07:18] Priya: Perfect. Also compliance around data retention — if we use hosted, can we set data retention windows?
[07:24] Jordan: Yes, hosted supports retention policies and log redaction; Dedicated/Private gives you full control. We'll note default retention is 30 days for hosted, configurable via contract.
[07:40] [10:00] Lena: Quick demo bit — here's a Python example for an embedding call: client.embed(texts=[...]) then you get vectors. We show sample batching for embeddings (batch_size: 64) to lower overhead.
[10:26] Priya: For embeddings we plan nightly batch jobs ~200k rows, any advice?
[10:31] Lena: For that scale, use Dedicated or use hosted with scheduled bulk windows; Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization and batching configs to cut cost. We'll include a sample runbook.
[11:00] Carlos: Are there limits per account? Like rate limits or token quotas?
[11:05] Jordan: Yes, hosted has rate limits and quotas; dedicated gives reserved throughput. We can provision rate limit exceptions for pilots.
[11:20] [20:00] Lena: Back to SDK specifics — environment variables: REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_ENDPOINT (optional), REDWOOD_REGION, REDWOOD_DEFAULT_MODEL. We also include a .env.example in the repo. For TypeScript we recommend using ts-node for the quick demo, and provide a Dockerfile.
[20:33] Priya: Can you walk through the typical auth flow in CI? We rotate keys often.
[20:38] Lena: CI pattern: store REDWOOD_API_KEY in your CI secrets (e.g., GitHub Actions secrets), ephemeral deploy keys for ephemeral envs, and for Dedicated use a short-lived service identity that is created via the control plane. We support SAML/SCIM for provisioning.
[21:00] Aisha: For VPC peering, what network info do you need?
[21:05] Jordan: We'll need CIDR ranges, peering or transit gateway preferences, and port allowances. For on-prem we do an appliance or the Private package.
[21:30] Priya: You mentioned benchmarks — what's the typical pilot size and duration?
[21:36] Jordan: Typical pilot is 2-4 weeks: run 1) SDK quickstart + sample app, 2) small benchmark (~10k requests across different seq lengths), 3) cost projection using Optimize. We can run the benchmark with you and provide scripts.
[22:00] Lena: I'll outline a benchmark script in the repo: sample payload generator, concurrency control (wrk or vegeta), and expected metrics to collect (p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU util).
[22:25] [30:00] Priya: Do you have an example of a retry/backoff strategy in the SDK? We use exponential backoff and jitter.
[30:05] Lena: SDK includes a retry policy module. Out of the box we use exponential backoff with configurable jitter and max attempts. For idempotent requests you can add request ids to dedupe. We'll include code snippets.
[31:00] Carlos: Any notes about model pinning and rollouts? We need predictable outputs for regulatory reasons.
[31:10] Jordan: You can pin model versions in the request or at the route level in the control plane. For rollouts we support canary and A/B tests in Redwood Console; Optimize can track eval regressions against saved prompts.
[32:00] Priya: For our legal team, we need an audit log export. How granular are logs?
[32:07] Jordan: Audit logs include token-level usage, request metadata, and control plane actions; retention is configurable. We'll send the schema.
[33:00] [40:00] Lena: Quick troubleshooting tips: if you see 504s at high concurrency, increase batching windows or move to Dedicated; look at KV cache hits to reduce repeated context.
[40:20] Aisha: How do we debug model quality regressions?
[40:25] Jordan: Use Redwood Optimize and the evals harness; save prompt sets and track model outputs, set regression alerts. We tie that to SDK tests.
[41:00] Priya: One more — do you have TypeScript typings and docs?
[41:05] Lena: Yes, full TS types shipped with the package and we publish API docs. We'll share the docs link and repo.
[42:10] [50:00] Jordan: Ok let's recap next steps and owners. I'll email the pricing and security pack. Lena will push the quickstart repo and benchmark scripts. Priya will send sample payloads and RPS. Aisha will coordinate network/VPC details.
[52:00] Sam: Thanks everyone, we might try the quickstart this week.
[52:15] Jordan: Great. We'll aim to have the repo and docs in your inbox by Monday.
[52:30] Priya: Thanks. Endorse.

References/Links mentioned: https://redwood.ai/docs/sdk-quickstart (repo), security pack (link to shared drive), perf deck (link to slides), benchmark scripts (attached in repo).

End of transcript.
